text:
The evidence can't say whether fire caused the loss. The tool explicitly states that it does not establish the cause of the change (harvest, fire, storm, or clearing).

What it does show:
- Hansen/UMD mapped about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021 within the asset (2.23% of its area). This is corroborated by later-year observations and by the JRC 2020 forest reference, which agrees on 98% of the event area.
- Most of the affected area (68.1 ha) is planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda), with no native forest. The remaining 13.2 ha lies outside mapped forest.
- Hansen loss includes any stand replacement, such as plantation cutting, so this could be routine harvest. That is only a possibility, not a finding.
- The forest map gives context, never cause.

To determine whether fire was responsible, you'd need separate evidence, such as burned-area products, fire alerts, or the owner's harvest records.
